# Proverbs 20 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A-mocker [is] wine, a-brawler [is] strong-drink, and-everyone going-astray by-it [is]-not wise.

**2** A-growling like-a-young-lion [is the]-terror-of a-king; one-provoking-him sins against-his-[own]-soul.

**3** Honor for-a-man [is] to-cease from-strife, but-every fool breaks-out.

**4** Because-of winter the-sluggard does-not-plow; he-asks in-harvest and-there-is-nothing.

**5** Deep waters [are the]-counsel in-[the]-heart-of a-man, but-a-man-of understanding draws-it-out.

**6** Many a-man proclaim each his-lovingkindness, but-a-man-of faithfulness who can-find?

**7** One-walking in-his-integrity [is] righteous; blessed [are] his-sons after-him.

**8** A-king sitting on-a-throne-of judgment scatters with-his-eyes all evil.

**9** Who can-say, 'I-have-made-pure my-heart; I-am-clean from-my-sin'?

**10** A-weight and-a-weight, an-ephah and-an-ephah — an-abomination-of YHWH, even both-of-them.

**11** Even by-his-deeds a-youth makes-himself-known — whether pure and-whether upright [is] his-work.

**12** [The]-ear hearing and-[the]-eye seeing — YHWH has-made even both-of-them.

**13** Do-not-love sleep lest you-become-poor; open your-eyes — be-satisfied [with] bread.

**14** 'Bad, bad,' says the-buyer, but-going-away then he-boasts.

**15** There-is gold and-abundance-of corals, but-a-precious vessel [are]-lips-of knowledge.

**16** Take his-garment, for he-has-become-surety [for a]-stranger; and-in-behalf-of a-foreign-woman seize-him-as-pledge.

**17** Sweet to-a-man [is] bread-of falsehood, but-afterward his-mouth is-filled [with] gravel.

**18** Plans by-counsel are-established, and-by-wise-guidance make war.

**19** One-revealing secrets [is one]-going as-slander; and-with-one-opening-wide his-lips do-not-associate.

**20** One-cursing his-father and-his-mother — his-lamp will-be-extinguished in-[the]-pupil-of darkness.

**21** An-inheritance gotten-hastily in-[the]-beginning — its-end will-not be-blessed.

**22** Do-not-say, 'I-will-repay evil'; wait for-YHWH and-He-will-save you.

**23** [An]-abomination-of YHWH [are] a-weight and-a-weight, and-scales-of deceit [are]-not good.

**24** From-YHWH [are the]-steps-of a-man; and-a-man — how can-he-understand his-way?

**25** A-snare for-a-man [is to]-say-rashly 'Holy!' and-after vows to-reconsider.

**26** A-king wise scatters [the]-wicked, and-turns upon-them [the]-wheel.

**27** A-lamp-of YHWH [is the]-breath-of a-man, searching all [the]-chambers-of [the]-belly.

**28** Lovingkindness and-truth guard a-king, and-he-upholds by-lovingkindness his-throne.

**29** [The]-glory-of young-men [is] their-strength, and-[the]-splendor-of old-men [is] gray-hair.

**30** Bruises-of a-wound scour-away evil, and-blows [scour] [the]-chambers-of [the]-belly.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **20:5**: Mayim amuqqim — 'deep waters.' The image of hidden counsel that must be drawn out like water from a deep well.

- **20:9**: Rhetorical question admitting universal human impurity. Anticipates the theology of Ecclesiastes 7:20 and Psalm 51.

- **20:27**: Ner YHWH nishmat adam — 'a lamp of YHWH is the breath/spirit of man.' The human spirit as God's internal searchlight — a profound anthropological statement.

— EMET
